sources.citation: Neethivanan, J. 1976. Survey of Kanauri in Himachal Pradesh (Census of India 1971, Series 1, Language Monograph No. 3). Delhi: Controller of Publications. [= A's work 11, re-reported because it is not entirely silent on tone]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: States (after Konow) that Kanauri lacks a tonal system; nothing on word stress; the phonology chapter proper (pp. 11-20) has no stress/tone section. For jang1254 this is not a statement (other variety, second-hand), hence reading none found for our languoid; for kinn1249 it would read 'no tones'.

sources.citation: Österreichische Akademie der Wissenschaften, Phonogrammarchiv. Project page 'Researching and Documenting Endangered Languages of Kinnaur' (contact Christian Huber), the Internet Archive 2026-01-03.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: States that systematic research on 'Shumcho/Humcho, Jangrami (both West Himalayish)' began 2001-2004 and that 'Jangrami (Ethnologue: Jangshung) is the language of the high caste in Jangi, Lippa and Asrang'; the publication list (Huber 2007, 2011, 2013, 2014, 2017 PhD, 2019, 2023) is entirely on Shumcho — no Jangshung publication.

sources.citation: Huber, Christian. 2007. Researching local languages in Kinnaur. In J. Ahamer & G. Lechleitner (eds.), Um-Feld-Forschung: Erfahrungen – Erlebnisse – Ergebnisse, 249-266. Wien: Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften.

Published data from the high caste language of Jangi, Lippa and Asrang is perhaps confined to the words collected in the Lippa entries of J. D. Cunningham's (1844: 225ff.) list of Thebarskad ("Tibberkad") words.' p. 256: the Jangi/Lippa/Asrang high-caste language = Ethnologue's Jangshung, 'not to be confused with the extinct Zhangzhung language'. p. 263: the OeAW project assembled a Jangshung vocabulary and texts, but publication focus was Shumcho.

sources.citation: Sharma, Devidatta (D.D.). 1988. A Descriptive Grammar of Kinnauri (Studies in Tibeto-Himalayan Languages 1). Delhi: Mittal Publications.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Describes Standard (Lower) Kinnauri only. p. 6 lists 'II. Thebarskad' as a dialect group 'in villages Lippa, Jangi, Asrang, Labang, Kanam, Sunnam, Namgya and Shaso' (i.e. Jangshung + Shumcho + Sunnam) with no data. pp. 45-46 '(v) Stress and Pitch': 'Kinnauri neither, like English, is a stressed language, nor, like Chinese, a tonal one.. Usually in a polysyllabic word the initial syllable has a higher stress and the non-initial a higher pitch. Being non-phonemic these features.. can occur in free variation' — a statement about Kinnauri (kinn1249, already in catalog), not about Jangshung.

sources.citation: Sharma, Bansi Ram. 1976. Kinnar Lok Sahitya [किन्नर लोक साहित्य]. Bilaspur (H.P.): Lalit Prakashan. Chapter 11 'लोक-भाषा', pp. 338-345 (dialect classification of Kinnaur incl. no. 8 'जंगी, लिप्पा तथा असरंग की बोली.. इसे जंगरामी कहा जा सकता है', and a Hindi story rendered in 25 local varieties incl. 'जंगरामी, असरंग गांव').
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No phonology. Prose limited to classification, Tibetan influence, mutual intelligibility and a general remark that the varieties differ in pronunciation ('उच्चारण सम्बन्धी भिन्नता'); then a c. 8-line connected text in Jangrami (Devanagari, scanned imperfect) parallel to the same story in Kinnauri, Chhitkuli, Thebar-skad (Kanam), Sunnami, Namgia and Nyam-skad versions. Text data only — no accent marks, no statement.

sources.citation: Negi, Thakur Sen. 1975. 'किन्नौरी बोलियाँ' [Kinnauri dialects]. Somasi 1(4), October 1975 (Shimla: H.P. Academy of Arts, Culture & Languages); reprinted in Kinnaur: Jeevan aur Sanskriti, Shimla: Himachal Academy of Arts, Culture and Languages, 2011, pp. 83-90.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No phonology content. Gives the seven mother-tongue areas of Kinnaur, then four Hindi sentences rendered in each variety incl. (ग) जंगरामी: 'कान गोवे देनिच तोन? / ज्ञम गोवे देनिच तोदम? (आदरसूचक)', 'चा तुड् / चा तुड्म', etc; §41 says Sunnami is closest to Thebar-kad and Jangrami and that Thebar[-kad] and Jangrami agree with each other more than with the rest 'but it cannot immediately be said that they are two sisters born of one mother'. Nothing on accent (बलाघात/स्वराघात) or tone.

sources.citation: Mamgain, M.D. (ed.). 1971. Himachal Pradesh District Gazetteers: Kinnaur. Simla: Government of Himachal Pradesh. Chapter 'People', section 'Language', pp. 69-75.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No phonology. Enumerates ten dialects, gives speaker figures, then 'ten sentences of each dialect with English rendering' — the Lippa/Asrang/Jangi set is printed in Devanagari (badly scanned in the archive.org text layer; legible in the PDF scan, 21 MB, not downloaded) — and notes 'No exhaustive and systematic survey of the languages and dialects of Kinnaur has so far been made'. Sentence data only, no accent marking or statement.
